cohort: The study included 2,288,589 persons born in Denmark between 1978 and 2017, of whom 63,191 were exposed to maternal preeclampsia.
finding: Offspring exposed to maternal preeclampsia and born at term had an increased risk of kidney disease in infancy and increased rates of most kidney disease subtypes after one year of age, with the strongest associations for chronic, unspecified, and diabetic kidney disease after 25 years of age, whereas preeclampsia with preterm delivery showed little association beyond the first year of life.
followup_time: Up to 47 years (cohort born 1978-2017, study published 2025), with specific analyses after 25 years of age.
gest_age: Included both term (37 or more weeks) and preterm (under 37 weeks) births, with analyses stratifying by gestational age.
